observability.description: Configure the Kasm observability stack (OpenTelemetry Collector + ClickHouse). Kasm services emit logs, traces, and metrics over OTLP to a Collector, which stores them in ClickHouse where they back the reporting UI. See Observability (./docs/observability.md) for architecture and sizing guidance.
observability.title: observability

enabled.description: Master switch for the whole observability stack. Set to false to deploy no Collector and no ClickHouse, disable the OpenTelemetry SDKs in every Kasm service, and serve a disabled browser-telemetry stub. Reporting features that read telemetry will return empty results.
enabled.title: enabled

collector.description: Configure the behaviour of the OpenTelemetry Collector tiers. Deployment settings for each tier live under `components.otelGateway` and `components.otelSidecar`.
collector.title: collector

gateway.description: Configure the single cluster-wide gateway Collector, which makes the trace-sampling decision and writes all telemetry to ClickHouse.
gateway.title: gateway

existingConfigMap.description: Name of a user-created ConfigMap holding a complete configuration for the gateway Collector, under the key `config.yaml`. Set this to take full ownership of the gateway config: the chart renders none of its own, and the values that only shape that config (`tailSamplePercentage`, `forward`, and `clickhouse.retention`) are ignored.
existingConfigMap.title: existingConfigMap

tailSamplePercentage.description: Percentage (0-100) of traces to keep after the always-keep rules. Traces containing an error, and traces slower than one second, are always kept regardless of this value. Applied at the gateway, which is the only tier that sees a whole trace.
tailSamplePercentage.title: tailSamplePercentage

forward.description: Forward a copy of all telemetry to an external OTLP/HTTP endpoint in addition to storing it in ClickHouse. Useful for shipping to a vendor or a central Collector. Applied at the gateway, so a forwarded copy reflects the sampling decision.
forward.title: forward

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP endpoint to forward to (e.g. `https://otlp-gateway.example.com/otlp`). Leave empty to disable forwarding.
endpoint.title: endpoint

token.description: Bearer token for the forwarding endpoint. Prefer `existingSecret` over putting a credential in values.
token.title: token

existingSecret.description: Read the forwarding bearer token from an existing Secret instead of `token`. Both `name` and `key` are required when used.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

upstream.description: Redirect the Kasm app services that export straight to the local gateway (currently API and the API worker pools; see kasm.otelEnv) to an external OTLP/HTTP collector instead -- e.g. a router in front of several Kasm releases. Collector sidecars (Proxy nginx, Connection Proxy, DB Postgres) are unaffected: they always export to this release's own gateway and are not rerouted by this setting. Leave empty to keep today's default (local gateway for everyone).
upstream.title: upstream

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP endpoint the API/API-worker exporters should send to instead of the local gateway (e.g. `http://otel-router.otel-router.svc.cluster.local:4318`). Leave empty to keep exporting to the local gateway.
endpoint.title: endpoint

token.description: Bearer token for the upstream endpoint. Prefer `existingSecret` over putting a credential in values.
token.title: token

existingSecret.description: Read the upstream bearer token from an existing Secret instead of `token`. Both `name` and `key` are required when used.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

clickhouse.description: Configure ClickHouse, the telemetry store that backs Kasm reporting.
clickhouse.title: clickhouse

enabled.description: Deploy a ClickHouse StatefulSet to store telemetry. Set to false to run the Collector with no telemetry store at all: signals are received and discarded, and Kasm reporting features return empty results. To use a ClickHouse you already run, leave this true and set `standalone` instead.
enabled.title: enabled

standalone.description: Setting standalone to true will prevent the deployment of the ClickHouse StatefulSet and requires you to have a ClickHouse server already set up and awaiting connections. Use the endpoint values below to connect to your external instance.
standalone.title: standalone

nativeEndpoint.description: DSN for ClickHouse's native interface, used by the Collector to write telemetry (e.g. `tcp://clickhouse.example.com:9440?secure=true&skip_verify=true`). A bare `host:port` is wrapped with the chart's defaults. Only used when `standalone` is true, and required together with `httpEndpoint`.
nativeEndpoint.title: nativeEndpoint

httpEndpoint.description: URL for ClickHouse's HTTP interface, used by Kasm to read reports and logs (e.g. `https://clickhouse.example.com:8443`). Only used when `standalone` is true, and required together with `nativeEndpoint`.
httpEndpoint.title: httpEndpoint

database.description: Name of the ClickHouse database holding Kasm telemetry.
database.title: database

username.description: ClickHouse user Kasm connects as. Also the writer credential used by the gateway Collector and the retention Job.
username.title: username

readUsername.description: ClickHouse user api uses to read reports, holding only GRANT SELECT ON <db>.* instead of `username`'s full access. When the chart manages ClickHouse (`enabled: true`, `standalone: false`), leaving this empty still gets you a read-only user: it defaults to `kasm_otel_ro`. For a `standalone` external ClickHouse, leaving this empty instead keeps api on `username` (no read-only user is rendered) unless you set this to a read-only user you have provisioned there yourself.

existingSecret.description: Read the ClickHouse password(s) from an existing Secret instead of the chart-generated `clickhouse-password`/`clickhouse-ro-password` keys. `name` and `key` (for `username`) are required together when used; `readKey` (for `readUsername`) is optional and falls back to `key` when unset, matching `readUsername`'s own fallback to `username`.

tls.description: Enable TLS on the bundled ClickHouse's 8443 (HTTPS) and 9440 (native) ports using the same certificate as the rest of Kasm, mirroring how the bundled Kasm DB is configured. Requires `certificate.secretName` or cert-manager. Has no effect when `standalone` is true.
tls.title: tls

caCert.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate trusted when connecting to a standalone ClickHouse over TLS (e.g. `httpEndpoint: https://...` behind a private or self-signed CA). Ignored for the bundled ClickHouse, which already uses the shared Kasm certificate. clickhouse_connect (the Python client Kasm's api uses) requires an explicit CA file - it does not consult SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or this chart's trustedCaBundle mechanism - so setting this renders a dedicated ConfigMap and mounts it into the api container. Leave empty to use the system trust store, or set `tlsVerify: false` to skip verification instead. Mutually exclusive with `caCertConfigMap`.
caCert.title: caCert

caCertConfigMap.description: Name of an existing ConfigMap containing the CA certificate for a standalone ClickHouse, under the key `ca.crt`. Use this instead of `caCert` if you already manage the certificate as a ConfigMap. Ignored for the bundled ClickHouse.
caCertConfigMap.title: caCertConfigMap

tlsVerify.description: Whether the api container verifies a standalone ClickHouse's TLS certificate at all. Set to false to skip verification (not recommended). Ignored when `caCert` or `caCertConfigMap` is set (an explicit CA always wins), and for the bundled ClickHouse, whose certificate is always verified.
tlsVerify.title: tlsVerify

This configuration is typically used for multi-region, large, or custom deployments where the customer requires a high degree of configurability and has multiple resources in disparate areas. allow_origin_domain.title: allow_origin_domain

Disabling DLP will disable many data loss prevention features enforced by Kasm, however, many of these features can be enforced by proper Group Policy in Windows. Disabling DLP will also break single sign on.
